description: Proposal (approved 2026-11-12): /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-3sy-typed-path.html. Constructing a struct calls the runtime once, to allocate by a size the compiler knows; every field store is emitted in place (raw word at 8 + slot*8, kind byte at its constant offset). The collector reads the kind byte (gc/trace.rs), so it is written on every store. Probe first: nothing may allocate between the allocation and the last store; if that cannot be shown the kind bytes alone are zeroed. Struct setters that lose their last caller are deleted. Signal: 363 (2 fields) and 1185 (8) instructions per construction today; re-measured on all three paths.
title: A struct is one allocation and stores in place
